A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cross-lingual context-retrieval study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original XQuAD evaluations, generation-error analyses, attribution and hidden-state measurements, and experiments with a finetuned LLaMA model.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Qwen model-size evaluations and Gemini-judged generation-error results. Its added Lingua accuracy table is explicitly attributed to external documentation.

M1.justification: The core procedures remain unchanged: perturbation-based oracle estimation, AttentionLRP attribution, Major Relevance Depth, cross-lingual hidden-state similarity, and the TULU-v3 finetuning control. Rewritten explanations do not establish a changed model or training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use XQuAD across the same 12 languages, with English-context/non-English-question and non-English monolingual scenarios, and TULU-v3 for finetuning. The added size and judge comparisons retain this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 expands the Qwen-2.5 comparison beyond the previously evaluated 7B and 72B models to include 1.5B, 3B, 14B, and 32B Base and Instruct checkpoints. The main multifamily comparator set remains unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a broader model-size experiment and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite as a second generation-error judge. Existing data and finetuning settings remain stable. Section 2.1.2 now states that exact match is not used, although appendix Table 6 retains exact-match results; this wording does not establish actual removal of that evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Qwen size-sensitivity analysis, a second-judge robustness check addressing possible Qwen self-evaluation bias, and an illustrative exact-match failure case. It removes the three en-superior hidden-state panels for LLaMA-3.1-Instruct-8B from v1 Figures 4–6; corresponding analyses for other models remain.

E5.justification: The MRD plots retain their existing error bars. v2 introduces no new repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty-reporting procedure, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The retained main performance, oracle, and appendix score tables preserve their values after renumbering. New results include the Qwen size sweep, such as mean en-x F1 of 67.64 for Instruct-14B, and Gemini-judged error rates in Table 9. Additional per-language error entries appear, while three en-superior hidden-state panels are omitted.

T1.justification: The 95% cumulative-relevance definition of MRD, cross-lingual cosine-similarity ratio, and error-rate equations remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims about competitive post-trained open models, two-phase question encoding and answer retrieval, the importance of post-training, and larger models' language gaps. Rewriting and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 shifts its explanation from languages' similarity to English toward language-dependent effects of demonstrations and the association between lower context similarity and better xMRC performance. v2 also adds an untested implication about steering middle-layer representations and recommends examining language resource levels.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 newly specifies that default system prompts and chat templates come from model tokenizer.config files. The detailed finetuning recipe, including hardware, training time, and hyperparameters, is retained from v1 Appendix B.3 in v2 Appendix C.3.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al. (2025), Tang et al. (2024), Wendler et al. (2024), and Zhao et al. (2024) to contextualize knowledge retrieval and multilingual mechanisms. It removes the brief survey of alternative attribution approaches and softens the related-work assertion that LLM xMRC had not been studied.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. The introduction clarifies different meanings of retrieval, mechanism sections are reframed around hypothesis and evidence, and the appendices are reorganized into experimental information, evaluation results, and mechanism analysis.

P2.justification: Plots throughout the main text and appendices are redrawn with revised labels and legends, and Figure 2 explicitly marks the two phases. v1 Figures 4–6 are consolidated into v2 Figure 4 with fewer panels. New Lingua and Qwen-size tables appear, and the generation-error table expands into separate judge panels.

improvement.justification: The Qwen size sweep and independent error judge provide useful targeted checks, while clearer explanations, prompt documentation, and redrawn figures improve accessibility and reproducibility. These gains modestly outweigh the loss of three en-superior panels and the inconsistent wording about exact-match evaluation. The principal methods, findings, and evidential limitations remain largely unchanged.
